source_binding.assignment_record_hash_scope: dispatch-intent binding; no separate assignment record is exposed by the blind capsule contract

items.title: Shared buffer and save authority are explicitly unified
items.statement: All mutation sources enter one typed transaction model, and each file path has one buffer, dirty flag, last-saved version, and save/retry authority across panes, previews, LSP, and agent flows.
items.impact: This is a strong non-gap that prevents split panes and mutation producers from becoming independent file authorities.

evidence.exact_quote: Save authority remains single-owner per file path: one shared buffer, one dirty flag, one last-saved version, and one authoritative save/retry path across split panes, preview surfaces, LSP apply-edit, and agent mutation flows.

items.title: Transaction ordering and partial multi-file mutation outcomes are unspecified
items.statement: The typed-source model does not define version tokens, serialization order, conflict precedence, cancellation boundaries, or compensation when user, agent, preview, LSP, watcher, and recovery mutations race; multi-file batches expressly produce separate per-buffer groups but have no atomicity or partial-failure contract.
items.impact: Different implementations can lose edits, apply stale patches, or leave only a subset of a multi-file assistant turn applied while still emitting a single receipt.

evidence.exact_quote: Single-file assistant mutation batches produce one logical undo group for that file; multi-file assistant mutation batches produce one thread/run receipt and one undo group per affected file buffer while preserving multi-group shared-buffer semantics.

items.title: File identity key is not normalized across path, project, worktree, remote, and routed subjects
items.statement: The document alternates between one buffer per file path, canonical paths, concrete worktree identities, remote authority, and route_target identities without one normative identity-key algorithm covering symlinks, case-folding, hard links, project reuse, remote hosts, and worktrees.
items.impact: The same backing file can accidentally receive duplicate buffers or the wrong save/watch/chat/diff authority, while distinct worktree or remote subjects can be collapsed.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Buffer:** In-memory representation of a file's content; one per file path. Edits apply to the buffer until Save.

Normal editor tabs are path-backed and file-watch-backed to one concrete file identity; PM must not implement a content-swapping tab that hides dirty state, undo history, save target, file-watch identity, or chat/diff routing.

items.title: Capability-pack activation lacks a lifecycle and authority model
items.statement: Detection and user override are required before durable settings mutate, but the spec does not define pack provenance/trust, permissions, dependency conflicts, activation rollback, re-indexing, unload behavior, or what happens to open state when a chosen interpretation changes.
items.impact: A project interpretation can enable incompatible or over-privileged modules and leave durable settings, indexes, and commands in an incoherent state after override or failure.

evidence.exact_quote: Project open MUST run explicit detection/import logic before enabling capability packs. When signals conflict, are incomplete, or match more than one project interpretation, the UI MUST surface the plausible interpretations and make autodetection visible and overridable before mutating durable project settings.

items.title: Index degradation is visible but freshness and fallback correctness are not testable
items.statement: Warm, rebuilding, missing, and unavailable index states must be shown, yet no state machine, freshness/version token, per-consumer capability matrix, stale-result invalidation rule, or latency/correctness oracle is defined for editor, tree, search, and symbol consumers.
items.impact: Surfaces can display a degraded badge while still serving stale or incomplete results as if they were current.

evidence.exact_quote: While an index warms, rebuilds, is missing, or is unavailable, affected surfaces MUST show reduced-capability/degraded-mode state and keep fallback behavior explicit rather than pretending the project is fully indexed.

items.title: Ordinary editor tabs cannot silently swap worktree variants
items.statement: The exact worktree rule keeps ordinary tabs bound to one concrete file and requires explicit compare or variant-open actions, with badges only where mixed worktree results appear.
items.impact: This prevents dirty state, undo, save, watcher, chat, and diff routing from being hidden behind a content-swapping tab.

evidence.exact_quote: The design bias is explicit: edit one concrete variant, compare across variants explicitly, switch variants deliberately, expose `Open other worktree version`, `Compare with worktree...`, and optional `/dropdown` selection only as explicit compare/open actions, and never hide worktree context behind a generic tab that silently changes identity.

items.title: Tree scale targets do not define complete-result or performance oracles
items.statement: The tree must list all project files and handle 10k+ rows, while each directory is capped at 10,000 and may use Show more or type-ahead; the spec does not define paging completeness, stable ordering under watcher updates, benchmark hardware, response budgets, memory ceilings, or behavior when a single directory exceeds the cap by orders of magnitude.
items.impact: A capped tree can satisfy rendering checks while silently omitting nodes or becoming unstable during refresh.

evidence.exact_quote: Virtualized tree handles 10k+ rows without freezing

**very large directories** (e.g. node_modules): virtualize by row, apply a row cap per directory (AutoDecision: 10_000 entries; key `file_manager/row_cap_per_directory`) with "Show more" or type-ahead to narrow

items.title: Bulk tree mutations lack complete destructive-action and path-serialization rules
items.statement: Multi-select delete is allowed with recursive confirmation and copy-full-path emits newline-delimited paths, but confirmation scope, symlink recursion, partial failures, open/dirty descendants, rollback, and filenames containing newlines are not resolved.
items.impact: Bulk deletion can remove an unintended recursive scope or become unrecoverable, and newline-delimited output is ambiguous for valid filenames containing newline characters.

evidence.exact_quote: `Delete` may operate on multi-select with recursive confirmation; `Copy full path` copies one absolute path for single-select or a newline-delimited list for multi-select.

items.title: External drag/drop has deterministic baseline direction and ordering
items.statement: Incoming and outgoing operations default to copy, Shift requests move, only folders/root accept incoming drops, and multi-item processing is lexicographic by normalized source path.
items.impact: The principal user action, valid target, and batch ordering are explicit rather than left to platform defaults.

evidence.exact_quote: **Default is copy** for both directions (safe, no accidental removal). AutoDecision: **Shift** modifier triggers **move** (copy then delete source on success) for both directions.

items.title: Shift-move can destructively delete external sources without an authority or acknowledgement contract
items.statement: Incoming Shift-move implies deleting a source outside the project, and outgoing drag delegates copying to another process, but the spec does not require explicit destructive confirmation, reliable target-completion acknowledgement, source revalidation, or policy checks before deletion.
items.impact: A modifier key can cause data loss outside the authorized project boundary, or PM can delete a source after a target app accepted URIs but did not durably copy them.

evidence.exact_quote: **Shift** modifier triggers **move** (copy then delete source on success) for both directions.
For **drag out:** The OS or target app performs the copy when it receives the file list/URIs; we only provide the paths.

items.title: Overwrite conflict behavior is undefined for directories and live buffers
items.statement: Always overwrite is selectable, but replacement-versus-merge semantics for directories, symlink conflicts, metadata preservation, open dirty buffers, watcher invalidation, and rollback after a partially overwritten tree are not defined.
items.impact: Two compliant builders can destroy, merge, or preserve different target contents under the same user-visible Overwrite choice.

evidence.exact_quote: "When dropping, if name exists" → **Always ask** | **Always overwrite** | **Always keep both (rename)**.

items.title: Exact authored strings lack a localization contract
items.statement: Expert/ELI5 variants and many exact English labels are required, but the document does not define stable message IDs, interpolation/plural rules, translated variant parity, locale-sensitive shortcuts, or layout/overflow acceptance for translations.
items.impact: Exact copy can drift between modes or break in translated layouts while still satisfying English-only checks.

evidence.exact_quote: Authored tooltip/help/hint copy defined by this plan must provide both Expert and ELI5 variants and follow the single checklist in `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` §7.4.0.

items.title: Accessibility and IME requirements are acknowledged but not falsifiable
items.statement: Keyboard support, accessibility, IME, selection, caret, clipboard, and input correctness are elevated to acceptance level, but there are no named assistive technologies, platform matrices, semantic roles, focus-restoration rules, composition-event cases, large-input cases, or pass/fail oracles.
items.impact: An editor can claim keyboard and IME support while failing composition, screen-reader tree navigation, or focus continuity on supported platforms.

evidence.exact_quote: The editor adapter must treat accessibility, IME, selection, caret, clipboard, cursor drift, paste behavior, `/editor-wrapper` limitations, and input correctness as acceptance-criteria-level behavior.

items.title: Symlink and path containment rules permit unresolved escape and race cases
items.statement: Incoming symlinks are copied without resolution while containment checks focus on the normalized target directory; the plan does not specify rejection or labeling of links that point outside the project, component-safe resolution, target-directory symlink policy, or race-resistant file-descriptor operations.
items.impact: A drop can install a project-internal symlink to external data or exploit a target swap between validation and mutation, undermining the project-root write guard.

evidence.exact_quote: When **copying in**, AutoDecision: copy the symlink as a symlink (do not resolve).
When **dropping onto** the tree, resolve the drop target to an **absolute path** and check that it is **under the project root** (e.g. `target.starts_with(project_root)` with normalized paths).

items.title: Cancel, partial failure, retry, and restart semantics are not one coherent transfer transaction
items.statement: The operation can be canceled, can continue after item failures, can retry failed items, and may be a move, but the spec does not define the commit point, cleanup of partial destination data, source deletion ordering, persisted receipts, idempotent retry, or recovery after app/OS crash.
items.impact: Cancel or retry can leave truncated files, duplicate copies, or a partially moved batch with no durable way to determine what completed.

evidence.exact_quote: Run copy (and optional move) in a **background task**; show progress and allow cancel.
If one of N items fails (e.g. permission denied), **continue** with the rest; at the end show a summary: "Copied N-1 items. Failed: {path} -- {reason}."

items.title: The immutable 5 MB cap contradicts the configurable 2-10 MB hard cap
items.statement: One sentence says a buffer must never exceed 5 MB, while the same sentence exposes a Hard cap setting whose example range reaches 10 MB; no precedence resolves whether 5 MB is absolute or merely the default.
items.impact: Builders and tests can enforce incompatible limits, and the GUI can offer a value the editor is forbidden to honor.

evidence.exact_quote: **Hard cap:** Never load more than **5 MB** into a single buffer. Above 5 MB, show "File too large to edit" and offer "View read-only (truncated)" or "Open in system editor." Configurable in Settings → Editor: **Large file threshold (lines)** (e.g. 5k-50k) and **Hard cap (MB)** (e.g. 2-10); persist in redb.

items.title: Tab LRU eviction does not protect dirty, locked, or recovery-bearing buffers
items.statement: Max editor tabs is described as capping tabs and buffers in memory with LRU eviction, but no eligibility, prompt, pinning, snapshot, write-lock, multi-view, or failure rule prevents eviction from discarding unsaved or unreconciled state.
items.impact: Opening one more tab can silently unload or lose a dirty, agent-written, or recovered buffer depending on implementation.

evidence.exact_quote: This caps how many tabs (buffers) are kept in memory; when exceeded, LRU eviction applies (§10.7).

items.title: Recovered remote edits cannot masquerade as a successful remote write
items.statement: Recovered remote-backed buffers are explicitly local-only, use exact banner copy, and must reconnect or revalidate the destination before save or flush can claim success.
items.impact: The UI cannot falsely imply that recovered local memory has reached the remote destination.

evidence.exact_quote: For recovered remote-backed buffers, the banner copy is: `Recovered local edits — remote destination not yet synchronized`.

items.title: Save conflict checks are vulnerable to a check-to-write race
items.statement: Changed-on-disk is checked on focus or before Save, but no expected-version token or compare-and-swap write is required at the actual atomic replace; remote recovered buffers similarly lack a base revision and three-way conflict rule after revalidation.
items.impact: A disk or remote change occurring after the prompt check but before write can be overwritten without a second decision.

evidence.exact_quote: **When to check:** On **Save** (before overwriting: prompt Reload / Overwrite / Cancel) and when the **editor pane or the file's tab gains focus**

items.title: Document-pane writing lock preserves the shared-buffer invariant
items.statement: Both document and file-editor views become read-only while the agent writes, streaming updates still enter the shared buffer, and release restores normal behavior without creating another history branch.
items.impact: The plan explicitly prevents dueling user and generation writes while keeping one source buffer.

evidence.exact_quote: Streaming updates from the agent still apply to the shared buffer so the user can watch content evolve.
This lock is an interaction rule only; it does not create a separate buffer or history branch.

items.title: Writing lock has no lease, owner identity, stall recovery, or forced-release rule
items.statement: The lock is tied to a status string and released when that status changes, but crash, disconnect, canceled worker, duplicate writer, stale event, and reconnect cases are unspecified, as are lock ownership and user recovery controls.
items.impact: A stale writing status can indefinitely lock the only authoritative buffer, while premature release can reintroduce dueling edits.

evidence.exact_quote: Once the doc leaves `writing…`, the lock is released and both surfaces return to normal edit/save behavior.

items.title: Stale rendered selections must fail instead of silently rebasing
items.statement: Annotations bind canonical source text and stale rendered-state mutation is explicitly rejected, while Send selection to chat remains adjacent composer state and does not mutate the buffer.
items.impact: This avoids attaching an annotation or chat selection to changed source without user awareness.

evidence.exact_quote: If a selection was made against stale rendered state, mutating annotation creation must fail explicitly rather than silently rebase to a different span.

items.title: Approval-scope revocation does not define cache and UI data lifecycle
items.statement: Open-file visibility is filtered by execution role and approval scope, but there is no rule for already-open tabs, buffers, recovery snapshots, undo history, clipboard, recent lists, indexes, previews, or notifications when access is revoked or a user changes.
items.impact: Restricted content can remain visible or recoverable after the approval scope that permitted it has ended.

evidence.exact_quote: The open-file list visible in the GUI is filtered by the active execution_role and the current approval_scope. Files opened in restricted approval scopes are not shown to unprivileged users.

items.title: Artifact envelope traversal has no precedence, cycle, or stale-reference rules
items.statement: OpenArtifact resolves artifact_id and follows several linked reference families, but ordering, missing-link behavior, cycle detection, conflicting envelopes, authorization checks at each hop, and content-hash revalidation are unspecified.
items.impact: Different resolvers can open different or unauthorized artifacts, loop through envelope links, or surface stale content under a valid artifact ID.

evidence.exact_quote: Use `OpenArtifact` for identity-native runtime-artifact opens: resolve `artifact_id` first, then follow envelope refs to `content_ref`, `linked_artifact_id`, `logical_artifact_id`, receipt-like refs, `attempt-level` evidence lineage, and Source Control, GitHub, Docker, or Kubernetes surfaces when relevant.

items.title: Mention picker does not explicitly inherit worktree and approval visibility filters
items.statement: Mentions preserve canonical file identity and are project-scoped, yet the picker contract does not explicitly include worktree_id, execution_role, approval_scope, remote-cache state, or mixed-root disclosure even though open-file and worktree rules require those distinctions elsewhere.
items.impact: A mention can select the wrong worktree variant or reveal a file that the active scope should not expose.

evidence.exact_quote: the inserted mention preserves the canonical file identity/path needed by prompt assembly and click-to-open behavior

items.title: Rendered preview inputs lack sandbox and resource-access requirements
items.statement: Markdown, Mermaid, HTML, SVG, image, and generated-document previews share identity, but this owner text defines no script policy, CSP/sandbox, local-file/network access, SVG external references, sanitization, decoder limits, navigation prompts, or trust labeling for untrusted workspace and artifact content.
items.impact: Opening a repository file or artifact preview can execute active content, read local resources, make network requests, or exhaust memory without a normative guard.

evidence.exact_quote: Markdown, Mermaid, HTML, SVG, image, and generated document previews use shared preview/session identity so chat, editor, browser, and FileManager links resolve to the same subject instead of opening unrelated panes.

items.title: Open targets and adjacent runtime owners are sharply bounded
items.statement: The PM-native target set is exact, system-default is a separate future handoff, and browser/terminal entrypoints remain placement and routing affordances rather than FileManager-owned runtime sessions.
items.impact: This avoids a hidden system fallback and prevents FileManager from absorbing browser and terminal session ownership.

evidence.exact_quote: `cmd.file.open_with` offers PM-native targets first: `source_editor`, `image_viewer`, `workspace_preview`, `detached_preview`, and `diff_review`. `system_default` is a separate future handoff through `cmd.file.open_in_system_default`, not the MVP fallback for PM-native open behavior.

items.title: Operational failures lack correlation, redaction, and support diagnostics
items.statement: Open and route failures are logged and surfaced, but the required record shape omits operation IDs, retry attempt counts, timing, endpoint/cache/version context, redaction rules, user-copy-to-support data, and retention, making cross-surface diagnosis non-deterministic.
items.impact: Users and support cannot reliably correlate a toast, concern error, fallback route, remote classification, and backend attempt without exposing sensitive paths ad hoc.

evidence.exact_quote: Log a visibility deferral (do not fail the entire run).
Emit a navigable error in the concern record so the user can inspect what went wrong.

items.title: Search, symbol navigation, diff, and Source Control ownership are explicit
items.statement: The continuation distinguishes FileManager rendering/routing from Search regex acceleration, LSP symbol data, FileSafe mutation safety, and Source Control git-native ownership, including correction of a stale Go-to-symbol owner reference.
items.impact: The plan avoids duplicating Search and git semantics under FileManager-local callbacks or stale section references.

evidence.exact_quote: It must not imply that the regex index owns File Manager search or symbol indexing; FileManager consumes search results and fallback labels while `grep` and Search regex acceleration stay under Tools and storage-plan.

items.title: F-002 preserves FileManager scope and owner deferrals
items.statement: F-002 names the owned user-facing surfaces and explicitly defers chat UX, layout, browser actions, and storage terms to their owner documents.
items.impact: The unit is a concise scope boundary rather than a claim of ownership over every adjacent subsystem.

evidence.exact_quote: FileManager owns the File Manager, in-app IDE-style editor, @ mention, click-to-open, image/HTML preview, tabs, and editor enhancement scope while deferring chat UX, layout, browser actions, and storage terms to their owner docs.

items.title: F-003 compresses several independently failing subsystems without dependencies or acceptance oracles
items.statement: Detection/import, override UI, indexing degradation, remote attachment, lazy loading, and performance are one split-recommended unit with empty dependency metadata and provenance-only validation, leaving sequencing and independently testable outcomes to builders.
items.impact: A later compiler cannot derive safe implementation order or discrete pass/fail checks for the unit's detection, index, remote, and loading branches.

evidence.exact_quote: File Manager/editor capability packs are activated by detected project signals after explicit detection/import logic, with plausible interpretations visible and overridable, indexing degraded states explicit, remote attachment state visible, and capability-pack breadth bounded and lazy-loaded.
depends_on: []

items.title: F-004 research constraints are broad but operationally unfalsifiable
items.statement: The unit bundles local-first remote operation, scanning, preview, recovery, widgets, Rust core, atomic save, watchers, and histories under lineage labels without measurable startup, memory, latency, crash, data-loss, or compatibility thresholds.
items.impact: Nearly any architecture can claim conformance to the research direction without demonstrating that the identified failure modes are prevented.

evidence.exact_quote: External discovery research-lineage anchors constrain the editor/File Manager toward local-first remote-capable operation, incremental scanning, first-class preview/manage operations, durable recovery, native diff/test/task widgets, reusable Rust text core, atomic save/watch handling, and explicit histories while rejecting known fragility modes.

items.title: F-005 archetype prohibitions lack concrete invariants
items.statement: The unit rejects ephemeral state, weak recovery, limited workspace models, and terminal ownership, but does not translate those archetype-level concerns into durable-storage, reconnect, workspace-count, synced-scroll, sanitization, or ownership acceptance criteria.
items.impact: The negative constraints are directionally useful but cannot reject a concrete implementation that repeats the named failure modes.

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master must not inherit ephemeral or memory-backed state, weak durable storage, reconnect/forced-refresh flows, limited multi-buffer/workspace models, no synced scrolling, sanitization shortcuts, or backend/API dependency risk as hidden defaults.

items.title: F-006 is incorrectly marked non-GUI despite user-visible input and pane behavior
items.statement: The unit covers selection, caret, split-pane undo behavior, degraded language fallback, and editor updates—directly user-visible interaction and state—yet gui_related is false and the reason claims it has no GUI presentation.
items.impact: GUI-aware planning and review lanes can omit F-006 even though its selection, caret, undo, and degraded-mode requirements must be implemented and visually verified.

evidence.exact_quote: The editor adapter stays thin: host/workspace owns file, project, runtime, execution transport, and project identity while the editor renders and edits; selection/caret, guarded updates, split-pane undo ownership, Unicode/revision transforms, degraded language fallback, and execution-transport separation remain explicit.
gui_related: false

items.title: F-002 through F-006 acceptance criteria validate migration form, not product behavior
items.statement: Their repeated acceptance criteria prove source preservation and PlanUnit addressability, while validation surfaces run migration/index checks; no scenario, state transition, error injection, UI assertion, security test, or performance threshold demonstrates the canonical behavior.
items.impact: Governance can report the PlanUnits valid even when none of their runtime or GUI requirements has executable evidence.

evidence.exact_quote: The covered source span remains losslessly available for exact-text audit.
python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate

items.title: F-007 establishes the local vocabulary
items.statement: The unit explicitly centralizes Buffer, Tab, Editor group, Dirty, Preset, redb, seglog, and FileSafe terms, with an owner note separating seglog and FileSafe responsibilities.
items.impact: The principal editor state terms have a discoverable local definition surface.

evidence.exact_quote: FileManager defines Buffer, Tab, Editor group, Dirty, Preset, redb, seglog, and FileSafe terms for the editor and File Manager surface.

items.title: F-008 is marked non-GUI despite directly governing undo and visible effective modes
items.statement: The unit's save/history/undo authority determines visible editor behavior, and its source span explicitly carries requested-versus-effective editor modes, yet gui_related is false; this also risks separating transaction implementation from its required GUI state projection.
items.impact: A GUI lane can miss undo-group, restore-history, dirty-state, and effective-mode behavior that the user must see and control.

evidence.exact_quote: All user, preview, agent, FileSafe/LSP, restore/revert, and recovery replay mutations enter the shared buffer through typed transaction sources before dirty state, undo grouping, and save authority update; one save authority per file path governs split panes, previews, LSP edits, and agent mutations.
gui_related: false

items.title: F-009 preserves core tree behavior and explicit failures
items.statement: The unit covers listing, open routing, virtualization, persisted expansion, ignored-file and row-cap settings, plus open, refresh, empty, and permission states.
items.impact: The core tree happy path and principal visible failures remain addressable in one unit.

evidence.exact_quote: The File Manager panel lists project files under root, opens selected files through the editor open-file contract, virtualizes large trees, restores expand/collapse state, exposes Hide ignored and row-cap settings, and shows explicit open/refresh/empty/permission error states.

items.title: F-010 makes cross-worktree compare identity explicit
items.statement: The unit retains project, repository, path, left/right worktree, and optional revision identity while forbidding a normal tab from hiding save/watch/undo/chat/diff identity.
items.impact: The compare/open handoff carries enough context to avoid whichever-tab-is-active routing.

evidence.exact_quote: Worktree-variant opens are identity-rich: same repo-relative path across worktrees defaults to side-by-side compare with project, repo, path, left/right worktree, and optional revision identity; ordinary tabs stay path-backed to one concrete file identity and must not hide dirty state, undo history, save target, file-watch identity, or chat/diff routing.

items.title: F-011 says keyboard accessibility but provides no interaction-state oracle
items.statement: The unit bundles docking, filtering, ignored styling, menus, selection, validation, reveal, and keyboard accessibility without defining tree roles, focus transfer after pop-out/redock, selection announcement, menu traversal, high-contrast state, or keyboard-equivalent acceptance cases.
items.impact: The implementation can include Arrow and Enter handlers yet remain unusable by keyboard or screen reader through detach, multi-select, menus, and reveal.

evidence.exact_quote: File Manager panel placement supports left/right dock or pop-out, optional detach/snap behavior, filter/search, .gitignore dimming or hiding, context menu entrypoints for canonical tree actions, active-row plus multi-select behavior, create/rename validation, reveal/current-file highlighting, and keyboard-only accessibility.

items.title: F-012 preserves Shift-move without resolving external deletion authority
items.statement: The PlanUnit accurately carries copy-default and Shift-move behavior but does not add the confirmation, external-source policy, completion acknowledgement, or rollback contract necessary for the destructive move branch.
items.impact: Standardization preserves an unsafe ambiguity as an accepted requirement rather than turning it into a testable guarded action.

evidence.exact_quote: File Manager external drag/drop supports dropping files/folders onto project folders with copy default, Shift-move semantics, valid drop target validation, tree refresh/progress, drag-out URIs for project files, and deterministic per-item handling for multi-select operations.

items.title: F-013 requires cancel but not cancellation semantics
items.statement: The unit mandates background progress/cancel alongside target validation and overwrite handling, yet its criteria and negative constraints say only that the UI thread must not block; they do not define safe points, destination cleanup, source deletion, or completion reporting after cancel.
items.impact: Cancel can mean stop scheduling, interrupt the current file, roll back, or merely hide progress, producing materially different data outcomes.

evidence.exact_quote: Drag/drop implementation uses platform file-drop APIs for Windows, macOS, and Linux, normalizes and validates target paths under the project root, provides conflict dialog or setting behavior, performs large copy/move in background tasks with progress/cancel, and shows visual drag target plus post-drop feedback.

items.title: F-009 through F-013 erase explicit sequencing behind empty dependency arrays
items.statement: The source says tree-open behavior requires the open-file contract and project context, while drag/drop relies on FileSafe and shared path rules, but every unit declares depends_on and unblocks empty; compilation therefore cannot enforce the documented prerequisites.
items.impact: A future node compiler can schedule tree, identity, or transfer work before the open, storage, mutation, and platform contracts it needs.

evidence.exact_quote: **Requires** §4.1 open-file contract before "select file opens it"; requires project context (project root).
depends_on: []

items.title: F-014 names many failure classes without defining their transactional outcomes
items.statement: The accepted unit names path limits, disk space, cancellation, rollback, permissions, locked files, symlinks, and background execution, but does not define preflight timing, cleanup guarantees, retry idempotency, move-source state, or per-platform pass/fail cases.
items.impact: Listing a failure class can be mistaken for specifying it, leaving destructive edge behavior incompatible across platforms.

evidence.exact_quote: Drag/drop gap handling covers cross-platform behavior, directory drops, move-versus-copy clarity, name conflicts, symlink policy, sensitive path exposure, cancellation, errors, locked files, path-too-long messages, project-root write guards, permission-denied errors, disk-space checks, rollback cleanup, and background execution.

items.title: F-015 changes optional move semantics into custom-sort reorder and marks deferred work accepted
items.statement: The governing prose describes optional drag-to-another-folder move and explicitly keeps copy as default even on the same filesystem; F-015 instead says internal reorder for custom sort and same-filesystem move fallback, adds drag-to-chat/show-hidden concepts, and remains an accepted requirement despite its deferred owner note.
items.impact: A builder can implement custom ordering or same-volume move behavior not established by the prose, while optional enhancements can be scheduled as accepted mandatory requirements.

evidence.exact_quote: **Drag to reorder within tree:** Allow dragging a file/folder to a different folder in the **same** tree to move it (reorder). Same security (target must be under project root); implement as move within project. Optional for MVP.

Deferred drag/drop enhancements include internal reorder for custom sort, same-filesystem move fallback, undo toast for recent copies, drag-to-chat attachment, and Settings options for default drop action, conflict policy, and show hidden files.

items.title: F-016 captures the editor MVP acceptance surface
items.statement: The unit retains open, save, dirty/read-only, large-file, transient-state, empty-file, canonical-path, cursor/scroll, and highlight-setting requirements.
items.impact: The principal editor MVP surface is not lost during PlanUnit standardization.

evidence.exact_quote: The in-app IDE-style editor MVP opens files from the open-file contract, saves buffers, shows dirty and read-only states, enforces large-file limits, shows transient states, handles empty-file behavior, preserves canonical paths, and records cursor/scroll payload shape and highlight duration settings.

items.title: F-017 strengthens optional tab reorder into unconditional support
items.statement: The prose requires reorder only if the design supports it, but F-017 states that placement supports reorder without retaining the condition, so the PlanUnit changes product scope rather than preserving it.
items.impact: Planning and implementation can treat an optional affordance as mandatory, creating scope and acceptance drift.

evidence.exact_quote: User can switch between open files, close a tab (with unsaved prompt if dirty), and reorder tabs if the design supports it

Editor placement uses the File Editor strip and supports docked visibility, detach/redock, one floating editor window, tabs with active-buffer switching, close/unsaved prompts, reorder, and persistence.

items.title: F-018 keeps save-related facts orthogonal
items.statement: Dirty, read-only, degraded, marker, lock, stale-disk, changed-on-disk, transient failure, and recovery attention are not collapsed into one vague status; save failure preserves dirty state and recovery actions.
items.impact: Users can distinguish why a file needs attention and a failed save cannot silently appear clean.

evidence.exact_quote: Editor save state keeps dirty, read-only, degraded, change-marker, write-lock, stale-disk, changed-on-disk, transient save/reload failure, and recovery attention as orthogonal facts; Save is explicit, save failure leaves dirty state intact with retry, save-as, and reason, and shared buffers remain authoritative.

items.title: F-019 is marked non-GUI despite defining visible restore actions
items.statement: The unit includes Restore to… / History and document-pane restore behavior that must be launched and observed in GUI surfaces, yet gui_related is false; this can exclude required GUI state, confirmation, error, and focus behavior from GUI planning.
items.impact: A non-GUI lane can implement backend restore routing without the required user confirmation and visible history surfaces.

evidence.exact_quote: Revert and restore flows route through explicit backend-owned restore history: cmd.chat.revert resolves target_message_id or latest assistant turn, whole-turn multi-file restores update each buffer via backend refresh notification, and document pane restore/history uses the same restore pipeline without owning separate restore points.
gui_related: false

items.title: F-020 requires revalidation but not remote conflict resolution
items.statement: The unit correctly forbids claiming remote success from local recovery, but does not bind the snapshot to a remote base revision or define the UI and data outcome when revalidation finds the destination changed, deleted, read-only, or moved.
items.impact: Reconnect can overwrite newer remote content or strand recovered edits without a deterministic compare, save-as, retry, or discard path.

evidence.exact_quote: Recover-unsaved is required for local and remote-backed buffers; recovered remote-backed buffers represent local unsaved memory only, show the exact recovery banner, and must reconnect or revalidate destination before save or flush claims remote success.

items.title: F-021 fixes the offline label and prevents pretend-live remote surfaces
items.statement: The live action is exactly Work offline (cached files only), the shorthand is compatibility-only, no-cache state must disable or disclose, and disconnected listings/search/diff/git/shell/LSP/write capabilities cannot present as live.
items.impact: Remote degradation is explicit and legacy shorthand cannot drift back into live copy.

evidence.exact_quote: File Manager/editor owns cached-file-only offline editing: live UI uses Work offline (cached files only), legacy Work offline (cached) is compatibility shorthand only, no cached snapshot disables or shows no-cached-files state, and remote degraded states disclose host, pending write, read-only, search, git, shell, LSP, and file write availability.

items.title: F-022 drops navigation-highlight lifecycle and accessibility behavior
items.statement: The detailed source says the range highlight clears on edit or cursor movement, can fade after a configurable delay, and may disclose EOF clamping; F-022 compresses this to highlight/clamp support without preserving lifecycle, announcement, focus, reduced-motion, or color-independent acceptance requirements.
items.impact: Implementations can satisfy the PlanUnit while leaving stale highlights, inaccessible range indication, or inconsistent clamping feedback.

evidence.exact_quote: Highlight stays until the user edits or moves the cursor; **optional fade** after a **configurable delay** (AutoDecision: default 5 s; Settings → Editor).

Editor display and navigation show line numbers, open and scroll to requested line/range data, highlight read-only ranges, clamp beyond-EOF requests, support go-to-line, and use basic syntax highlighting with LSP semantic highlighting augmentation or fallback.

items.title: F-023 preserves split-group view and buffer ownership
items.statement: Each editor group has its own tab list and active tab, open defaults to the focused group, the file buffer is shared, and cursor/scroll state is per view.
items.impact: The PlanUnit distinguishes per-view navigation state from the single authoritative buffer.

evidence.exact_quote: Split editor panes are MVP scope with multiple editor groups, one tab list and active tab per group, one shared buffer per file path, focused group open targeting by default, optional Open in other group/new group actions, and per-view cursor and scroll state.

items.title: F-024 has no recovery path for a stale or failed writer lock
items.statement: The unit combines shared-buffer authority, read-only lock projection, banner, and streaming updates, but provides no lock token, writer identity, heartbeat, disconnect state, timeout, cancel, retry, takeover, or rollback behavior when streaming stops mid-write.
items.impact: The only buffer can remain permanently read-only or contain an unexplained partial generation after a worker failure.

evidence.exact_quote: Embedded document pane shares the same file buffer, dirty state, save authority, restore pipeline, and history model as File Editor; when DocumentPane status is writing…, File Editor and document pane are write-locked/read-only for user edits with a visible lock banner while streaming updates still apply.

items.title: F-025 is incorrectly classified non-GUI
items.statement: Annotations, Send selection to chat, composer-prep state, and explicit stale-selection failure are direct GUI interactions and feedback, yet gui_related is false and the classification says this is only a state boundary.
items.impact: GUI planning can omit annotation affordances, selection handoff, and the required visible stale-state failure.

evidence.exact_quote: Embedded document annotations and chat handoff share document identity and buffer state while keeping annotation and composer-prep state adjacent to, not part of, file buffers: annotations anchor to canonical source text, send selection to chat does not mutate the buffer, and stale rendered selections fail explicitly.
gui_related: false

items.title: F-026 gives dirty plus changed-on-disk one explicit decision
items.statement: One buffer and dirty model is retained, Revert prompts before discard, and a dirty plus changed-on-disk condition must be one combined Reload/Overwrite/Cancel prompt rather than two sequential dialogs.
items.impact: The user receives one coherent conflict decision and does not face contradictory sequential prompts.

evidence.exact_quote: Editor data model uses one buffer per file path and no duplicate tabs per group; dirty state reflects in-memory versus last-saved content, revert prompts before discarding dirty data, and file-changed-on-disk checks on save or focus show one combined prompt for dirty plus changed-on-disk cases.

items.title: F-027 preserves explicit-save and read-only reason behavior
items.statement: Per-buffer undo, clipboard, wrap/font, UTF-8, line endings, explicit Save, binary/read-only handling, and visible reason strings remain in the PlanUnit, with no autosave and no MVP hex view.
items.impact: Users are told why editing is blocked, and saving cannot occur as an undeclared autosave side effect.

evidence.exact_quote: Editor text behavior includes per-buffer undo/redo, selection and clipboard, optional word wrap, monospace font, UTF-8 editable text, line-ending preservation, explicit Save only, binary/read-only file handling, and user-visible read-only reasons.

items.title: F-021 through F-027 remain provenance-valid but behavior-unverified and dependency-free
items.statement: Every unit repeats source-preservation acceptance and migration/index validators while depends_on/unblocks remain empty, despite remote, LSP, shared-buffer, document-pane, chat, storage, and watcher seams; no executable oracle proves the user-visible or failure behavior.
items.impact: The units can pass governance before their remote, GUI, concurrency, recovery, and integration behavior is implemented or proven.

evidence.exact_quote: The behavior is addressable through this fine-grained PlanUnit instead of broad F-001 coverage.

top_risks: External Shift-move can delete sources outside the project without an authority or reliable completion contract.
Symlink and check-to-use races undermine the stated project-root write guard.
Buffer/file identity is not normatively unified across paths, worktrees, remotes, routes, and filesystem aliases.
Save, recovery, writer-lock, and multi-file transaction races lack versioned conflict and rollback semantics.
The absolute 5 MB buffer limit directly conflicts with a configurable hard cap up to 10 MB.
Approval-scope revocation and rendered-preview content lack complete privacy and untrusted-input lifecycle rules.
PlanUnit acceptance and validation prove migration/index form, not product behavior, while dependency metadata remains empty.
F-006, F-019, and F-025 are materially misclassified as non-GUI; F-008 is also GUI-affecting.
strong_non_gaps: One shared buffer and one save authority per file path are explicit.
Ordinary tabs cannot silently swap worktree variants.
Recovered remote edits cannot claim remote synchronization before reconnect/revalidation.
Stale rendered annotation selections must fail rather than silently rebase.
PM-native open targets and browser/terminal/Source Control ownership boundaries are explicit.
Dirty plus changed-on-disk uses one combined decision prompt.
Offline cached-file wording and pretend-live prohibitions are exact.
synthesis.unknown_unknowns_assessment: Risk remains elevated because broad archetype and research-lineage units are accepted without concrete invariants, dependency metadata, executable behavior oracles, or lifecycle models for cross-process and remote failure. Unspecified platform drag acknowledgement, filesystem aliasing, preview execution, and access-revocation propagation are likely sources of emergent failures.
